punchline: Kiyosaki's rich dad called Robin Hood a crook and described a corporation as a file folder in a lawyer's office.
thirty_sec: Kiyosaki's rich dad tells a short history of tax. It started as a wartime stopgap, became permanent in England in 1874 and in the US in 1913, and slowly spread from the rich to everyone else. His big contrast is about order. An employee earns, gets taxed, then lives on the rest. A corporation earns, spends, and is taxed on what's left. When Robert's father said climb the ladder, rich dad asked why not own it. Critics warn that some of those deductions can be illegal.
